| [LIT-005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md) | Adding causality to the information-theoretic perspective on individuality | Bourrat (2024), DOI-10.1007/s13194-023-00566-1. The information-theoretic individuality measures of Krakauer et al. (2020) are associative, not causal. Replacing the observed past state with an intervened-on one (interventionist, Pearl-style) gives a causal information-theoretic measure of individuality, which the author applies to evolutionary transitions in individuality. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract on 2026-09-25; not read in full |

(2022), [ARXIV-2205.11595](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.11595). This introduction to the theme issue proposes no new result. It surveys emergence from quantum matter to epidemics, adopts Chalmers/Bedau "weak emergence" as the scientifically relevant notion, and sketches an operational definition of emergence from local rules plus initial conditions. | [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) v2 | Greater than the parts: a review of the information decomposition approach to causal emergence | Mediano et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2111.06518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06518). A review, with no new theorem, of the ΦID theory of causal emergence. A supervenient feature V_t is k-th-order causally emergent iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0. A system hosts such features iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0 (cited as Rosas et al. 2020, Theorem 1), and Syn⁽ᵏ⁾ = D⁽ᵏ⁾ + G⁽ᵏ⁾ (downward causation plus causal decoupling). The review's own additions are interpretive: the formalism is neutral between Granger and Pearl, coordinate dependence is defended as a feature, and it rebuts the charge that the theory makes no macro-versus-micro comparison. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-010); a short, accurate map of the ΦID emergence formalism and the right entry point to Rosas et al. 2020, which a reader will still need for the proofs, the assumptions and the redundancy-free practical criteria. None of these is stated in the review. |
| [LIT-027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md) v2 | Emergence as the conversion of information: a unifying theory | Varley et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2104.13368](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13368). Varley and Hoel apply a PID, with the Williams–Beer I_min redundancy, to past→future mutual information and summarise it with a new layer-weighted "synergy bias" B_syn ∈ [0,1]. Coarse-graining can raise B_syn at the macroscale. A macroscale XOR reaches 0.833, against 0.52 for its NAND/AND/OR implementation. In 200 random 3-node "Gaussian" TPMs expanded into equivalence-class micro/mesoscales with *identical* MI, every macroscale had higher B_syn, by ≈ 0.01–0.07 (r = 0.819 against macroscale B_syn). In 185 near-deterministic systems the change was mostly negative, down to ≈ −0.1. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-020); a clear, small-scale demonstration that coarse-graining can change the redundant/synergistic composition of information and not just its amount. It is worth reading as the explicit cross-scale counterpoint to the ΦID account (item 21). Its "unifying theory" is a framing: the EI section re-describes a known decomposition and contains no new result. |
